executive_summary: This collection window (March 30-April 5, 2027) is the forty-first archived window. The FW27-28 women's ready-to-wear fashion month remains closed and Haute Couture Spring/Summer 2027 remains unconfirmed as having occurred, consistent with the prior nine windows and with FHCM's published calendar (scheduled for late January 2027; no reachable post-show coverage was found this window either). The one new item this window is 'Glamoratti,' an 1980s power-dressing revival named in Pinterest's annual Predicts trend report and subsequently amplified across multiple editorial outlets. This is logged as a new, distinct signal (glamoratti-revival) rather than folded into last window's ss27-trend-forecast, since it originates from a social platform's first-party data product rather than a commercial forecasting outlet, and is a season-agnostic annual aesthetic call rather than terminology for a specific upcoming collection season. Medium confidence, emerging volatility, social_amplified origin. Per SKILL.md workflow note 10, the Wales Bonner/Hermes debut and CFDA Fashion Fund/Awards questions were checked briefly but not re-litigated as top signals: searches surfaced only already-known appointment/team-building coverage and no new CFDA announcement, both remaining untracked pending new information. `collection_status` is set to "thin" again: fashion month remains closed, and the only in-window discourse independently verifiable is a single platform-originated aesthetic-term signal.

top_signals.name: 'Glamoratti' 80s power-dressing revival surfaces via Pinterest Predicts data
top_signals.evidence: Pinterest's annual Predicts trend report names 'Glamoratti' -- an 1980s power-dressing revival built around sculpted-shoulder suiting, funnel-neck jackets, metallic fabrics, and deliberately unsubtle jewelry -- citing platform search-volume increases (self-reported by Pinterest: '80s luxury' up 225%, 'baggy suit' up 90%, 'chunky belt' up 65%, 'gold cuff' up 50%). This is distinct from the SS27/Resort 27 commercial-forecast terminology logged last window (ss27-trend-forecast, WGSN/Trendalytics-style labels for an upcoming season): Glamoratti is a season-agnostic annual aesthetic call originating from a social platform's own first-party data product, subsequently picked up and amplified across multiple editorial outlets (Marie Claire, Grazia, and others) framing it as a pullback from 'quiet luxury' toward overt glamour.
top_signals.index_note: New signal_id, distinct from poetcore-aesthetic (2026-07-20, an unrelated literary/preppy aesthetic already archived) and from ss27-trend-forecast (2027-03-29, commercial forecasting-outlet terminology for an upcoming season). Glamoratti is a Pinterest Predicts-originated, editorially-amplified aesthetic label, not designer- or runway-originated. Checked existing signal_ids across all reports before assigning -- no collisions.
top_signals.human_editor_note: Pinterest Predicts is the platform's own first-party trend report (an official data product, not scraped or manually sampled UGC), consistent with the compliant-sourcing requirement in SKILL.md workflow note 6. Search-volume percentages are self-reported by Pinterest and not independently audited, so this is logged as editorial-amplified social signal at medium confidence rather than upgraded on the strength of the editorial pickup alone -- editorial covering a platform's own trend report is not independent corroboration of the underlying data. Recommend a human editor re-check whether this term recurs in designer-origin or runway content once FW27-28/SS28 collections become reachable.
